name: Snert (Dutch Split Pea Soup)
ingredients: 1 hock - Smoked Pork Hock (left over ham hock is great)
1 tsp - Maggi Aroma (or use 1 maggi cube), use more for stronger flavour, but taste as you go
instructions: Soak peas overnight for at least 12 hours in cold water
After soaking, add pork hock, bay leaves, salt to the peas and water
Bring mixture to boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer
Cover soup and allow to simmer for 2 hours
While simmering, chop leeks, cauliflower into 2cm pieces
Chop carrots and celery into 1cm pieces
After the 2 hour simmer, add the veggies and meat to the soup and simmer for another 15 minutes or until tender
Remove the pork hock from the soup and cut the meat off the hock. Put the meat back in the soup and discard the hock.
Remove the bay leaves. Add Maggi, salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for another 20-30 minutes to thicken the soup up. If too thick, add water and allow for the sausage to cook through
The soup is suppose to be thick, not quite thick enough to hold a spoon up.

additional_context.source: Cooking Dutch Cookbook, heavily modified by Tori's Oma
additional_context.story: Snert is a traditional Dutch split pea soup that is thick and hearty and perfect for cold weather. Fun fact: snert is a highly contentious meal in Tori's family, approx 50% love it, the other 50% hate it. Luckily Tori and Isaac are both in the love it camp (thank goodness).
additional_context.tips: Serve with bread and butter. Snert is better the next day as the flavours meld together.
